How many H-1B petitions were made by Virginia employers classified under the Wholesale Trade industry during 2025?
In 2025, 59 H-1B petitions were filed by employers classified under the Wholesale Trade industry located in Virginia, according to data provided by the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services via the H-1B Employer Data Hub.
Employers classified under the Wholesale Trade industry based in Virginia submitted 59 H-1B petitions during 2025, according to data provided by the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services via the H-1B Employer Data Hub.
Of these, 57 were approved (96.6%), while two were denied (3.4%).
Employers are classified under industries based on their reported operations and may be involved in multiple industries.
The average approval rate for H-1B petitions across the United States in 2025 stood at 97.9%, lower than 2024's 98%. Statewide, Virginia employers across all industries submitted 29,682 petitions during the same period, achieving an approval rate of 98.2%.
The Retail Trade industry led the H-1B filings in Virginia during 2025, with 14,250 petitions (48% of all submissions), and an approval rate of 98.6%. Meanwhile, the Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services industry was the second largest contributor, filing 6,599 petitions (22.2% of the total), with an approval rate of 97%.
The Virginia employers which made the most petitions in the Wholesale Trade sector during 2025 included Kerecis, LLC with six petitions and Ferguson Enterprises, LLC with five petitions.
Compared to 2024, the Wholesale Trade sector in Virginia saw a 40.5% increase in the number of H-1B petitions during 2025.
The United States admits around 1 million legal immigrants annually, most of whom receive permanent residence (green cards) through family sponsorship or employment-based visas. In 2023, about 1.2 million immigrants were granted green cards, a return to pre-pandemic levels. Temporary visa programs, such as the H-1B for highly skilled workers and H-2A for seasonal agricultural workers, also play a critical role in filling workforce needs.
Public opinion on immigration varies, with 46% of Americans favoring maintaining current legal immigration levels, according to a 2024 Pew Research Center survey. Additionally, 42% believe that highly skilled workers, such as scientists, doctors, and programmers, should be prioritized for legal immigration, compared to 25% who prioritize workers filling labor shortages and 19% who emphasize family sponsorship. Despite this, family sponsorship remains the most common path to permanent residency, accounting for 63% of green cards issued in 2023.
